tradeoff: Sentence chunks hold one fact each, so a citation points at exactly the supporting sentence and an extractive answer quotes nothing extra. They lose context when a fact spans sentences, which the pronoun-merge rule only partly recovers. Fixed-size windows keep neighbouring sentences together and tolerate unpunctuated text, but they cut facts mid-sentence, dilute term scores with unrelated words, and make quoted answers carry text the question did not ask about.
